news.headline: Perimeter Debuts At Intermountain Health With FDA-Approved AI System For Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Industry trade press picked up Perimeter's first commercial deployment, framing Claire as the first PMA-approved, AI-enabled intraoperative margin assessment system to move from clinical trials into routine surgical practice. The coverage extended the news cycle into the week of the Q2 report and coincided with a further sharp move in the shares.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Deploys Claire OCT System to Aid Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Follow-up coverage of the launch added the first user feedback from the operating room, with Intermountain breast surgeon Dr. Teresa Reading saying Claire was simple to fold into her workflow and that the AI quickly directed her attention to areas of concern. Workflow fit is the key adoption question for a device that has to run inside a live lumpectomy.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Brings Perimeter's Claire™ to the Operating Room, a Landmark in Breast Cancer Surgery Using AI
news.summary: Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire, now live at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital under a systemwide agreement covering Intermountain's network. This is the first real commercial placement since March's FDA PMA approval, and the shares jumped roughly 11% on the news.

news.headline: Perimeter Schedules Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call for August 20th
news.summary: Perimeter confirmed it will report Q2 2026 results after market close on Thursday, August 20, with a conference call and webcast at 5:00pm ET. This will be the first quarterly update carrying management commentary on the Intermountain Health launch and on cash burn since the spring financings.

news.headline: Brookline Capital Markets Initiates Perimeter at Buy, PT C$1.54
news.summary: Analyst Kemp Doliver started coverage with a Buy rating and a C$1.54 (US$1.11) target against a C$0.32 close, citing Claire's Breakthrough Device status as a tailwind for a faster CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision expected by year-end. The note models well above 9% lumpectomy penetration by 2035.

news.headline: Paradigm Capital names Perimeter and maintains Profound as healthcare Top Picks
news.summary: Paradigm Capital added Perimeter as a healthcare Top Pick with a Speculative Buy rating and a C$0.95 price target, with the stock at C$0.275 at the time. The analyst frames the March FDA approval of Claire as the accelerant for U.S. commercialization and flags M&A optionality, noting the stock trades far below comparable MedTech takeout multiples.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 financial results
catalysts.detail: Perimeter reports Q2 2026 results after market close on August 20, with a call and webcast at 5:00pm ET. Watch for the first commentary on the Intermountain Health commercial launch, conversion out of the qualified-lead funnel, Claire pricing/recurring-revenue model, and cash burn versus the roughly C$7.5M LIFE offering and C$6.0M convertible placement raised in the spring.

catalysts.label: Expansion of Claire across the Intermountain network
catalysts.detail: Claire is currently live at only two Intermountain sites (LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital) under a systemwide agreement. Roll-out to additional Intermountain hospitals would be the cleanest near-term evidence that the first customer scales rather than stalls at a pilot.

catalysts.label: Additional U.S. hospital system placements
catalysts.detail: With Intermountain live as the first commercial deployment, the market is watching for a second and third named U.S. health system to sign from Perimeter's pipeline of qualified leads in the Prospecting/Developing/Validating/Contracting stages. A second system would establish that the Intermountain deal is repeatable.

catalysts.label: CMS New Technology APC / reimbursement decision
catalysts.detail: Management is pursuing a CMS New Technology APC pathway under the Medicare Outpatient Prospective Payment System for AI-enabled intraoperative OCT margin assessment, aided by Claire's Breakthrough Device Designation. Brookline's July note flagged a decision expected by year-end 2026; this is a company/analyst expectation rather than a confirmed CMS date, and it is the single biggest driver of Claire's U.S. adoption economics.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results – first quarter with Claire revenue
catalysts.detail: The Q3 print (typically reported in November) would be the first full reporting period after the August launch and the first chance to see actual Claire-related revenue and gross margin, versus the ~US$3.0M trailing-twelve-month revenue base built on the legacy S-Series.

catalysts.label: Possible Nasdaq up-listing
catalysts.detail: Cited by sell-side analysts as a potential catalyst to broaden U.S. institutional access following FDA approval and commercial launch. No official timeline has been announced by the company and it would likely require a consolidation and additional capital.

pulse: Perimeter has just delivered the proof point its whole 2026 thesis rested on: on August 13 Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire, moving the only FDA-approved AI-enabled breast-margin device from trials into live operating rooms, and the trade press (Medtech Insight, ITN) carried the story through the following week with encouraging first-user workflow feedback. The stock ripped on it - roughly doubling from the low-C$0.20s in early August to about C$0.45 on August 17 - before cooling to around C$0.37 on August 19 for a market cap near C$60M, with four analysts now at Buy and an average target around C$1.60 (Brookline C$1.54, Paradigm C$0.95). Everything now hinges on the August 20 Q2 report: with only two hospitals live, trailing revenue under US$3M and a ~US$16M annual net loss against spring financings of roughly C$13.5M combined, investors need to see funnel conversion and a credible cash runway - and beyond that, the CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision analysts expect by year-end remains the structural swing factor for this high-beta micro-cap.
